about: Deterministic NPI (create-cards-with-AI) guided-flow invariants. Each case mocks one model turn (mockModelResponse) plus any tool results it depends on (conversationHistory / context), and the harness runs it through the real exported deterministic functions (parseOperationRequest, validateOperation, resolveArrangementCodeFromHistory/Context) plus per-invariant detectors. `expect.violates` declares whether the mocked turn is a clean example (false) or a freelancing one the detector MUST catch (true). This mirrors the --mock-llm philosophy: mock the model, assert the deterministic layer. The live model is exercised by --live-llm.

invariants.1: A PA / arrangement code must come from a resolve_offer_selector or list_products tool result (or context) — never invented from the conversation.
invariants.2: A 32-char hex Offer ID is NEVER passed as list_products searchText; it must go through resolve/get_offer_by_id first.
invariants.3: resolve/get_offer_by_id -> list_products(searchText = resolved PA code) chaining is mandatory for Offer-ID and OSI inputs; the flow must not stop at the resolve step nor pass the raw identifier.
invariants.4: Already-selected-product short-circuit: when the turn carries arrangement_code: / 'Selected product:' / context.selectedProduct.arrangement_code, do NOT re-run list_products or re-render productCards — go straight to offering-type.
invariants.5: Empty list_products -> a legible 'couldn't find that product' message, NOT a crash and NOT a fabricated product.

cases.description: A product NAME passed as list_products searchText is not a fabricated code — names are legal lookup input.
Model jumps to create_release_cards with an arrangement_code no tool result ever returned.
A bare 32-hex Offer ID resolves via get_offer_by_id, never list_products.
A 32-hex Offer ID passed as list_products searchText returns garbage fuzzy matches and must be caught.
After a resolve result carrying product_arrangement_code, the next turn chains list_products with that exact PA code.
